data.title: SLB Seen Benefiting From Higher Oil Production Investment
data.description: According to CNBC, energy trader John Arnold said the underlying supply backdrop for oil was already bullish, while the article argued that refiners are the biggest beneficiaries of the current disruption because crack spreads, or refining margins, have never been wider. It said refiners could continue to post record profits for several years, though their share prices are already at record highs, and noted that oil service companies have rallied but are not yet at all-time highs. The piece said SLB is the largest of those oil service companies and that longer-dated long calls financed by shorter-dated short strangles are the preferred trade.

data.title: Alphabet Shows Signs Of Stabilization After May Correction
data.description: According to CNBC, Alphabet (GOOGL) has been in a corrective phase since May but is starting to stabilize as oversold conditions ease. Fairlead Strategies' Katie Stockton and Will Tamplin said the stock has rallied after a counter-trend buy signal from the DeMARK Indicators on Thursday, reclaiming support near its 200-day moving average around $337. They said the daily chart has improved, with stochastics turning higher and the MACD flashing a buy signal, while initial resistance is near $376 and final resistance is near $402. The analysts said a decisive break below the 200-day moving average would be a long-term setback, while the stock remains in a secular uptrend above its rising monthly cloud model.

data.title: VIX Jumps to 18 as Traders Favor AI Risk Over Fed Volatility
data.description:
According to CNBC, the Cboe VIX Index jumped to 18 on Monday, and options trading on the gauge rose to more than double the 30-day average volume as semiconductors and data-center stocks weighed on the S&P 500. By midday, three of the top five VIX contracts to buy were calls, and the biggest trade of the day was someone buying at least $3.6 million of 31-strike calls expiring in mid-November.

The move came after the VIX erased two days of gains on Friday even as inflation data pushed the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at this week's meeting to 90%. By Friday's close, options on the S&P 500 were pricing a 0.8% swing into weekly contracts expiring Sep. 18, below the 50th percentile of volatility expected for weeks with an FOMC meeting, according to analysis from New York-based options manager Carrick Lane. John Marshall, principal at Carrick Lane, said the market appears more comfortable with higher rates and is focusing more on AI than on interest-rate risk. He said equity investors seem to think the FOMC decision is already set and are treating AI as a more immediate concern.

The Merrill Lynch Option Volatility Estimate (MOVE) Index, which tracks volatility in U.S. Treasuries, rose 10 points last week to a 92nd percentile high, according to a note from Cboe head of derivatives market intelligence Mandy Xu. Marshall's analysis also showed volatility pricing for rate-sensitive assets such as the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) and the Vanguard Real Estate Index Fund ETF (VNQ) in the upper 90th and 80th percentiles. Even so, those bond-market signals have not been driving stock volatility, and odds of a hike on Wednesday's meeting rose above 91% by midday as equity prices firmed.

data.title: BitFuFu Produces 174 BTC in August, Up More Than 55% From July
data.description:
BitFuFu produced 174 BTC in August, marking an increase of more than 55% from July. According to NS3.AI, CleanSpark's production rose around 1% to 593 BTC, while Canaan's production fell roughly 4% to 44 BTC.

Canaan also sold 3,952 ETH and 54 BTC during the month. The figures highlight mixed monthly production trends among the miners.

data.title: UK Government Plans Public Acquisition of Speciality Steel UK
data.description:
The UK government is developing a plan to nationalise Speciality Steel UK, the country's third-largest steelworks, Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds told MPs, according to BBC. Ministers are looking to acquire the company, which has sites in Stocksbridge and Rotherham in South Yorkshire and Wednesbury in the West Midlands, after deciding not to back a bidder earlier this year over concerns about financing and protections for taxpayers.

Speciality Steel UK, which employs about 1,300 people, was taken into government control last year after the High Court forced its former owner, Liberty Steel, into liquidation. Production at the business was paused several months ago and staff were put on furlough on reduced wages. Reynolds said any future decisions and spending commitments would be subject to due diligence and funded from existing government budgets.

data.title: US House Speaker Johnson: AI Executive Talks Planned for This Weekend or Early Next Week
data.description: According to Sina Finance, U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson said he will meet with executives from artificial intelligence companies this weekend or early next week to discuss AI risks, and said it will take some time to develop related legislation. Johnson made the remarks at the U.S. Capitol.

data.title: U.S. Banking Groups Urge Senate to Tighten Stablecoin Reward Limits
data.description:
Eight U.S. banking groups urged the Senate to strengthen the Clarity Act’s restrictions on stablecoin interest and rewards. According to NS3.AI, the groups sent a letter to John Thune and Chuck Schumer on Monday ahead of the Senate vote on Tuesday.

The banks argued that crypto companies could use rewards that function like interest to attract customer funds away from traditional banks. They called for tighter limits as lawmakers prepare to vote on the measure.

data.title: AI | Cohere CEO Warns Frontier Labs Against Safety Standards 'Cartel'
data.description:
Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said proposals for the biggest frontier AI labs to coordinate on safety standards could entrench dominant players and amount to a "cartel," according to Bloomberg.

Gomez said tougher safeguards, independent testing and greater transparency are needed, but argued the rules should be shaped by a broader group of stakeholders rather than companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI alone.

data.title: AI | Roblox Expands Build as Baszucki Says AI Will Increase Game Creators
data.description:
Roblox is expanding its AI-powered creation tools with Roblox Build, which lets users create games directly from its mobile app, according to Bloomberg.

Chief Executive Officer David Baszucki said AI will lead to more creators, not fewer, as tools for generating code, 3D scenes and avatars make game development more accessible. He made the comments on Bloomberg Tech with Ed Ludlow.

data.title: STOCKS | Roblox Shares Jump 11% After New Developer Tools Announcement
data.description:
Roblox Corp. shares climbed more than 11% on Monday after the company announced new tools for game designers and new features for players at a developer conference on Sept. 11, according to Bloomberg.

The update was unveiled at the event as Roblox expanded its offerings for developers and users.

data.title: Robinhood Stock Tokens to Add Physical Redemption and Voting Features, Vlad Tenev Says
data.description: Robinhood co-founder and CEO Vlad Tenev said the company’s stock tokens will soon support physical redemption and voting features. According to Odaily, Tenev made the remarks in a recent statement.

data.title: UBS Adds Senior Hires to US Investment Bank Industrial Team
data.description: UBS Group AG has hired a series of senior bankers for its investment bank to strengthen industrial coverage in North America, according to a memo seen by Bloomberg.

data.title: ECB's Cipollone Says €200 Note Still Has Role Despite Laundering Risks
data.description:
European Central Bank Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said concerns about money laundering should not stop issuance of a €200 bill, according to Bloomberg.

He said there are now better ways to clean up illicit earnings than using banknotes.

data.title: U.S. President Donald Trump Says He Plans $5,000 “Trump Dividend” for All Adults
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. is reaping trillions of dollars in economic gains, investment, and major success, and plans to distribute a $5,000 "Trump dividend" to all adults nationwide, a proposal criticized by Democrats who want it blocked but Trump said it will be implemented.

data.title: Trader Unipcs Says He Will Not Sell EMBER Holdings Despite Short-Term Volatility
data.description:
Trader Unipcs said his investment thesis for EMBER remains unchanged and that he will not sell his position because of short-term volatility. According to Odaily, his EMBER holdings are worth about $687,500, with unrealized gains of about $271,700.

Unipcs previously said EMBER has shown strong resilience near its all-time high even as the broader market remains weak. He also said he would not be surprised if the token continued to rise sharply after returning to its all-time high, and added that some negative discussion around the Bubblemaps cluster and its partnership with Meteora has been overstated by the market.

data.title: Fed Overnight Reverse Repo Usage Falls to $1.42 Billion
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Federal Reserve overnight reverse repurchase agreement usage was $1.42 billion on Monday, with four counterparties, down from $5.255 billion in the previous trading day.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Apple launches Siri AI, starts English beta rollout
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Apple launched Siri AI and began rolling out an English beta version today, with expansion to five languages planned; the feature will not initially be available on iOS, iPadOS, or watchOS in the European Union.

data.title: AI | Parmy Olson Says Anthropic’s Safety Push Falls Short
data.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson says Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has talked about leading a “race to the top” in setting vigilance standards for others building powerful systems, but that ideal was probably impossible from the start, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Oil Tanker Rates Top $1 Million a Day as Strait of Hormuz Risk Cuts Supply
data.description:
The cost of hiring an oil tanker on the industry’s benchmark route rose above $1 million a day for the first time, according to Bloomberg.

The surge came as the Iran war left too few ships willing to cross the Strait of Hormuz to pick up cargoes.
